Project KO11 Is Proof That Geely Wants To "Knock Out" Range Rover, Launches Next Year in Europe
14 photos
Photo: Geely
Geely concluded its press conference at the 2026 Paris Motor Show with a "one more thing" announcement: Project KO11. The vehicle is not new, being known as the Geely Cruiser 700 in China, but its name bears more significance than the car itself. If you wonder what KO means in Project KO11, it's exactly what Geely plans for rival off-road brands like Range Rover and Toyota.
Chinese carmakers took over this year's Paris Motor Show, with no less than 20 brands on display. Geely seized the opportunity to make its first group-level appearance at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. The highlights were the Geely Monjaro EM-i, the Link & Co 07GT, and the Zeekr 9X. However, the most talked-about show car was the "Project KO11," introduced as a "One more thing" at the show.
For those familiar with the Chinese car market, the Project KO11 looks identical to the Geely Cruiser 700, also known as Battleship 700, depending on the translation. It's a proper off-roader designed to rival the Land Rover Defender. Scratch that, it's actually designed to destroy it, which explains the "KO" in the Project KO11's name.
The only reason why Geely hasn't introduced the KO11 as the Cruiser 700 is that it hasn't yet settled on a name for the EU-bound model. Cruiser 700 might get it into hot water with Toyota's legal department, while Battleship 700 is not a great name for Europe, no matter how you spin it. What's certain is that the name won't matter, because it would pose mortal danger to the Land Rover Defender regardless.
The Chinese name reveals that the Project KO11 is a 7-Series model, which means it sits just below the flagship models. This means it will provide all the creature comforts someone expects from a luxury 4x4 vehicle. The design is typical for a classic off-roader, with a boxy shape, high hood line, and a swing-out tailgate with a spare wheel mounted on it.
Photo: Geely The KO11 is underpinned by the Geely Terrain Architecture (GTA), which uses an integrated frame construction. This combines a unibody structure with a heavy-duty cage frame, saving space and weight while maintaining high torsional rigidity. The Geely Cruiser 700 / Project KO11 is the first model to use this architecture.
The Chinese model uses an EREV powertrain that combines a 2.0-liter gas engine with three electric motors for a total of 1,113 horsepower in its most potent configuration. The 70-kWh Golden Brick battery uses Geely's Short Blade cells and promises up to 217 miles (350 km) of pure electric range based on the CLTC cycle. Lesser configurations are also offered, including a smaller battery and a 1.5-liter engine.
These configurations will most certainly not make it into Europe, due to local emission regulations that basically exclude EREVs. This means that the Project KO11 will be converted into a PHEV off-roader, unless Geely decides to ditch the combustion engine altogether and launch it with a bigger battery as an all-electric off-roader. Not impossible, but it would certainly compromise on range, as the Jeep Recon EV showed us already.
The Chinese Geely Cruiser 700 is already on the market, with prices starting at 179,800 yuan ($26,800) for the base model. This is powered by a single electric motor and uses the 1.5-liter gas engine as a range extender. Australia will also get the EREV off-roader under the rather strange name of Battleship 700. Europeans, on the other hand, will have to wait another year before Project KO11 launches.
